items.title: Barry Kernfeld interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 16, 2020
items.q: what did I just see — Monica Zetterlund with the Bill Evans Trio at a rehearsal in 1966.

ctx.x: Well as I said, I regret that I wasn’t a whole bunch older to have experienced that stuff in the clubs, but how does that make me feel? There was this great New York City exhibit on Rembrandt and all the disputes about what he painted and what he didn’t paint, and this really cynical thing up on the wall, it said, “Every generation gets the Rembrandt that it deserves.” And I’m thinking well maybe every generation gets the jazz that it deserves. It’s just what we are. It’s not a choice that we can make. I just…

government broadcasting. They have these huge archive things, repositories of films and videos that are now being posted on the web for free because it’s a national thing, it’s not a commercial ownership thing. And I am seeing completely amazing performances that I’ve never seen before. So in a way I am now closer to that world than I ever was, if I can go and watch somebody, you know, what did I just see — Monica Zetterlund with the Bill Evans Trio at a rehearsal in 1966. They just knocked me out. One of the…

Well I don’t have to ask that question now. Sometimes I do ask that question, of time travel, but you just took care of it already. So in your role as an editor you’ve done so much of it. I wonder if it’s sometimes hard for you if there’s an artist that really demands attention and of course should be included whether it’s the book or the on-line edition, but you don’t particularly care for their music. Do you recognize that you might need to hand this off to somebody else or does it affect the way you think…
